title: The Frog Prince
author: Brothers Grimm
source: Public domain. Retold from the Brothers Grimm.

characters.name: The King
characters.voiceHint: a firm but fair royal voice

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, there was a princess who loved to play with a golden ball. Every day she tossed it high in the air beside the cool well in the palace garden. But one day the ball slipped through her fingers — plop! — straight down into the deep, dark well.

segments.speaker: princess
segments.text: "Oh no! My golden ball! I would give anything to have it back!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then, a big green frog poked his head out of the water.

segments.speaker: frog
segments.text: "Anything, princess? I do not want your pearls or your crown. But if you will let me eat from your plate, and sleep on your pillow, and be your friend — then I shall dive down and fetch your golden ball."

segments.speaker: princess
segments.text: "Yes, yes, I promise!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: said the princess. But secretly she thought a frog could never climb out of the well to follow her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The frog dove deep, deep down and came up with the golden ball in his mouth. The princess snatched it up with delight — and ran straight back to the palace, quite forgetting her promise.

segments.speaker: frog
segments.text: "Wait! Princess, wait for me!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: croaked the frog. But she was already gone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That evening, as the royal family sat at dinner, there came a curious sound at the door — splish, splash, splish, splash — and then a little knock.

segments.speaker: frog
segments.text: "Princess, princess, open the door! Remember the promise you made by the well!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The princess turned quite pale.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The king asked what was the matter, and the princess told him everything.

segments.speaker: king
segments.text: "My dear, a promise is a promise. If you gave your word, you must keep it. Go and let your friend in."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the princess opened the door, and the frog hopped in — splish, splash — right up to the table.

segments.speaker: frog
segments.text: "Lift me up beside you, and push your golden plate a little closer, so we may eat together."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The princess wrinkled her nose, but her father gave her a look, and she did as she was asked. And to her great surprise, sharing her dinner with the polite little frog was not so terrible after all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When dinner was done, the frog yawned a wide froggy yawn.

segments.speaker: frog
segments.text: "I am tired now. Please carry me upstairs and set me on your pillow."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The princess did not want to at all. But she remembered her promise, and this time she kept it kindly, carrying the frog gently up the stairs and setting him softly on her pillow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the moment she was kind to him with her whole heart — POOF! The frog vanished, and in his place stood a young prince with friendly eyes. A jealous witch had turned him into a frog long ago, and only a true friend could break the spell.

segments.speaker: prince
segments.text: "Thank you, princess! You kept your promise, and you set me free."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The prince and the princess became the best of friends, and in time, when they were grown, they were married. And ever after, the princess kept every promise she made — even the ones she made to frogs.
